title: Descent of chain maps between affine perfect complexes
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, F : I → CRing a functor, i₀ ∈ I, and A the colimit of F [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let E₀ and K₀ be cochain complexes of F(i₀)-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], each zero outside a finite interval and with each term finitely generated and projective. For i ≥ i₀ write Eᵢ and Kᵢ for their termwise scalar extensions along F(i₀ → i), and E and K for their termwise extensions along the colimit inclusion F(i₀) → A. For base-change maps between these complexes, use the canonical associativity transport [def-pc-complex-scalar-extension-hom]. Every chain map f : E → K is the canonical scalar extension of a chain map g : Eᵢ → Kᵢ at some i ≥ i₀.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.29.2, Tag 09RE, affine proof

proof.text: Each finite projective term of E₀ and K₀ is finitely presented, by Mathlib Module.finitePresentation_of_projective. Apply the map clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to the components fⁿ : Eⁿ → Kⁿ in the finite support of E₀, and take a common upper stage above i₀. Put zero components in the other degrees. For a preorder, use the same presentation-matrix proof of the cited lemma: the lifting and equality detection require only directedness and the elementwise colimit criterion [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], not antisymmetry. To use the stated partial-order theorem literally, quotient I by mutual comparability and select representatives. The resulting partial-order category is equivalent to I; F sends mutually comparable indices to inverse isomorphisms, so transport F and its colimit across this equivalence, apply the partial-order theorem, and transport the finite-data result back. Directedness supplies an upper bound with the original requested index.

The chain-map equations d_K fⁿ = fⁿ⁺¹ d_E hold after extension to A. Apply the equality-detection clause of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent-affine] to these finitely many equations between maps with finitely presented source and target, and take one common later stage. Outside the support the source is zero, so the equations are automatic. The components now define a chain map. Canonical scalar-extension associativity and componentwise extensionality identify its extension with f.

lean.statement: theorem affine_perfect_chainMap_descent {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (i₀ : I) (E₀ K₀ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} (F.obj i₀)) ℤ) (hE : (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (E₀.X n)) ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite (F.obj i₀) (E₀.X n) ∧ Module.Projective (F.obj i₀) (E₀.X n)) (hK : (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (K₀.X n)) ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite (F.obj i₀) (K₀.X n) ∧ Module.Projective (F.obj i₀) (K₀.X n)) (f : ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E₀ ⟶ ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (colimit.ι F i₀).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K₀) : ∃ (i : Set.Ici i₀) (g : ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj E₀ ⟶ ((ModuleCat.extendScalars (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K₀), scalarExtensionHom (F.map (homOfLE i.property)).hom (colimit.ι F i.val).hom (colimit.ι F i₀).hom (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.w F (homOfLE i.property)).symm) E₀ K₀ g = f
